# freewordcounter.app

A free online word counter and character counter that runs entirely in the browser. No login, no cloud, no tracking.

## Key Facts

- Counts words, characters with spaces, characters without spaces, sentences, paragraphs
- Shows reading time (200 wpm) and speaking time (130 wpm)
- Top 10 most frequent words analysis
- 100% free, no ads, no premium tier for counting
- No account required
- Text stored in browser localStorage only
- Works offline (PWA with service worker)
- Single HTML file, loads in under 200ms
- Dark mode, font size control, copy stats to clipboard

# Home — Free Word Counter & Character Counter Online — No Login Required

https://freewordcounter.app/

freewordcounter.app is a free online word counter and character counter that runs entirely in your browser with no login required. Paste or type any text and instantly see your word count, character count (with and without spaces), sentence count, paragraph count, reading time, and speaking time. freewordcounter.app works offline, stores nothing on any server, and loads in under 200ms as a single HTML file under 50KB. Unlike most word and character counters that are cluttered with ads and pop-ups, freewordcounter.app is clean, fast, and distraction-free. It also shows your top 10 most-used words and average sentence length — useful for writers, students, and SEO professionals who need to analyze their text quickly.

## What features does freewordcounter.app offer?

freewordcounter.app provides real-time text analysis the moment you start typing or paste content into the editor. The tool instantly calculates your word count, character count with spaces, and character count without spaces — all displayed as separate, prominent statistics. Character count is displayed both with and without spaces to serve different use cases: Twitter/X character limits include spaces, while some publishing platforms count only non-space characters.

Beyond basic counting, freewordcounter.app detects sentences and paragraphs in your text, giving you a complete structural overview. Reading time is calculated at 200 words per minute (average adult reading speed), and speaking time at 130 wpm (average presentation pace). The word frequency analysis reveals your top 10 most-used words, excluding common stop words, so you can identify repetition and improve your writing.

freewordcounter.app counts up to 100,000+ words without lag thanks to efficient browser-based processing. The app includes dark mode for comfortable writing in any lighting condition, font size controls to adjust the editor text size, and a copy stats button that copies all your statistics to the clipboard in one click. All preferences and your text are saved to localStorage so everything persists between sessions. freewordcounter.app also works offline as a Progressive Web App — once you visit the site, it caches locally and functions without an internet connection.

## How does this free word and character counter work?

Using freewordcounter.app takes three simple steps. First, open freewordcounter.app in any web browser — there is no signup, no download, and no installation required. The tool works in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge on both desktop and mobile devices.

Second, paste your text into the large editor area, or start typing directly. The editor supports any length of text and automatically saves your work to your browser's local storage.

Third, your statistics appear instantly in the panel beside the editor, including word count, character count with spaces, character count without spaces, sentence count, paragraph count, reading time, speaking time, average word length, average sentence length, and your top 10 most frequent words. All stats update in real time as you continue editing — there is no submit button and no delay.

## Why is freewordcounter.app better than other word counter apps?

freewordcounter.app is built for speed and simplicity. The entire application is a single HTML file with no external dependencies beyond fonts, meaning it loads faster than any competitor. There are no ads cluttering the interface, no pop-ups interrupting your work, and no cookie consent banners to dismiss. The clean, minimal design lets you focus entirely on your text.

Unlike wordcounter.net and similar tools, freewordcounter.app requires no login and no account creation. Your text never leaves your device — it is stored only in your browser's localStorage and is never transmitted to any server. This makes freewordcounter.app the most privacy-respecting word counter available.

freewordcounter.app shows character count both with and without spaces as equally prominent core statistics. This distinction matters for Twitter/X posts (280 characters including spaces), SMS messages (160 characters), and meta descriptions (155 characters). Many competing tools only show one character count variant, forcing users to manually calculate the other.

freewordcounter.app works fully offline after the first visit, functions as an installable Progressive Web App, supports dark mode, and lets you adjust the editor font size. Combined with instant real-time updates and a copy stats feature, freewordcounter.app delivers a better experience than wordcounter.net, charactercountertool.com, and wordcounter.io.

## Is freewordcounter.app private and safe to use?

freewordcounter.app is designed with privacy as a core principle. All text you enter stays in your browser via localStorage and is never sent to any server. There are no cookies, no tracking pixels, no analytics that collect personal data, and no third-party scripts beyond Google Fonts for typography. freewordcounter.app cannot read your text because there is no server to send it to.

The application works fully offline after the first page load, thanks to its service worker. This means even your network requests stop after the initial visit. freewordcounter.app is safe for confidential documents, academic work, business communications, and any text you want to keep private.

## What is a good word count and character count for different types of writing?

Different formats have different length requirements, and both word count and character count matter depending on the platform. Tweets and X posts are limited to 280 characters including spaces, which typically translates to 40 to 50 words. SMS messages have a 160-character limit per segment. Meta descriptions for SEO should be 150 to 155 characters to avoid truncation in search results.

Professional emails typically range from 50 to 200 words for maximum effectiveness. Blog posts perform best at 1,000 to 2,500 words for SEO purposes, with long-form content of 2,000+ words tending to rank higher in search results. College essays vary from 500 to 5,000 words depending on the assignment, with common formats being the 500-word short essay and the 2,500-word research paper. Novels generally run 70,000 to 100,000 words, with genre fiction sometimes running shorter and literary fiction occasionally running longer.

All modern browsers: Chrome 4+, Firefox 3.5+, Safari 4+, Edge 12+.

**How accurate is the reading time estimate?**
freewordcounter.app calculates reading time at 200 words per minute, which is the average adult reading speed according to research. Speaking time uses 130 wpm.

# freewordcounter.app vs WordCounter.net: Free Alternative

https://freewordcounter.app/vs-wordcounter-net.html

WordCounter.net is one of the most well-known word counting tools on the internet, and for good reason. It has been around for years, offers a wide range of text analysis features, and has built a strong reputation among writers and students. However, WordCounter.net comes with ads, requires an internet connection, and sends your text to its servers for processing. freewordcounter.app is a simpler, privacy-first alternative that runs entirely in your browser with no ads, no login, and no server-side processing.

## How do these two word counters compare?

The comparison covers the features most users care about when choosing a word counter tool. WordCounter.net has a broader feature set overall, including keyword density analysis and readability scoring. freewordcounter.app focuses on the core counting features that the majority of users need, delivered in a faster, cleaner, and more private package.

Feature comparison:
- Word count: Both ✓
- Character count (with spaces): Both ✓
- Character count (without spaces): Both ✓
- Sentence count: Both ✓
- Paragraph count: Both ✓
- Reading time: Both ✓
- Speaking time: Both ✓
- Top 10 word frequency: Both ✓
- Keyword density: WordCounter.net only
- Readability score: WordCounter.net only
- No ads: freewordcounter.app only
- Works offline: freewordcounter.app only
- Text stays in browser (privacy): freewordcounter.app only
- Dark mode: freewordcounter.app only
- Font size control: freewordcounter.app only
- Copy stats to clipboard: freewordcounter.app only

## What does WordCounter.net do well?

WordCounter.net deserves credit for being a reliable, full-featured word counter that has served millions of users. Its keyword density tool is genuinely useful for SEO professionals who need to see how often specific terms appear as a percentage of total content. The readability scoring, which includes Flesch-Kincaid and other indices, helps writers gauge the complexity of their prose. WordCounter.net also offers a browser extension and has a clean enough layout for a tool that relies on advertising revenue.

## Why choose freewordcounter.app instead?

freewordcounter.app is the better choice for users who value speed, privacy, and a clean interface. The entire application loads as a single HTML file under 50KB, making it significantly faster than WordCounter.net. There are no display ads, no pop-ups, and no cookie consent banners. Your text never leaves your browser — everything is processed locally using JavaScript and stored in localStorage. freewordcounter.app also works fully offline after the first visit, which is useful for users who write on planes, trains, or in locations with unreliable internet.

freewordcounter.app shows character count both with and without spaces as two separate, equally prominent statistics. This matters when writing for platforms like Twitter/X (280 characters including spaces), SMS (160 characters), or meta descriptions (155 characters). The dark mode toggle, font size controls, and copy stats feature make freewordcounter.app more comfortable for extended writing sessions.

## Who should stick with WordCounter.net?

If you rely on keyword density analysis or readability scoring for your work, WordCounter.net is the more feature-complete option today. SEO professionals who need detailed keyword percentage breakdowns will find WordCounter.net more suited to that specific workflow. freewordcounter.app currently focuses on core counting and timing features, though readability scoring is planned for a future update.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Is freewordcounter.app really free compared to WordCounter.net?**
Yes. freewordcounter.app is completely free with no ads, no premium upsells, and no login required. WordCounter.net is also free to use but displays advertising throughout the interface.

**Does freewordcounter.app have the same features as WordCounter.net?**
freewordcounter.app covers the core features most users need: word count, character count with and without spaces, sentence count, paragraph count, reading time, speaking time, and word frequency analysis. WordCounter.net offers additional features like keyword density and readability scores.

**Can I use freewordcounter.app offline unlike WordCounter.net?**
Yes. freewordcounter.app is a Progressive Web App that works fully offline after the first visit. WordCounter.net requires an active internet connection.

**Is my text private on freewordcounter.app?**
Yes. freewordcounter.app stores text only in your browser's localStorage. Nothing is ever sent to a server. WordCounter.net processes text server-side for some of its advanced features.

# Free Word Counter for Essays

https://freewordcounter.app/word-counter-for-essays.html

Meeting an essay word count requirement is one of the most common reasons people use a word counter. Whether you are writing a 500-word short essay, a 650-word Common App personal statement, or a 2,500-word research paper, freewordcounter.app gives you an instant, accurate word count the moment you paste or type your text. The tool runs entirely in your browser — no login, no ads, no distractions.

## Why do essay writers need a word counter?

Most essay assignments come with strict word count requirements. Going over the limit can result in point deductions, and falling significantly short suggests insufficient depth. A dedicated word counter gives you a precise count that you can trust, without the overhead of opening a word processor. freewordcounter.app shows your word count as the single most prominent statistic in its dashboard, making it impossible to miss.

Beyond raw word count, freewordcounter.app provides several statistics that are directly useful for essay writing. Paragraph count helps you verify that your essay has the right structural breakdown. Sentence count and average sentence length help you assess whether your writing has good variety — essays with consistently long sentences tend to be harder to read, while too many short sentences can feel choppy. The reading time estimate, calculated at 200 words per minute, helps you gauge whether your essay will take an appropriate amount of time for a reader to process.

## What are the typical word counts for different types of essays?

Essay word counts vary significantly depending on the type of assignment and the academic level. A standard short essay or reflection paper typically runs 500 to 750 words. The Common App personal statement has a 650-word maximum, which is one of the most well-known essay word limits in education. High school essays often range from 300 to 1,000 words depending on the subject and assignment type.

College-level analytical essays and argumentative papers usually fall between 1,000 and 2,000 words. Graduate-level research papers and term papers commonly range from 2,500 to 5,000 words. Thesis chapters and dissertations can run 8,000 to 15,000 words per chapter. freewordcounter.app handles all of these lengths without performance issues, counting up to 100,000+ words without lag.

## How do you check your essay word count with freewordcounter.app?

Open freewordcounter.app in any browser on any device. Paste your essay text into the editor area — or type directly into it. Your word count, character count (with and without spaces), sentence count, and paragraph count appear instantly in the stats panel. All statistics update in real time as you continue editing. There is no submit button, no loading spinner, and no waiting. freewordcounter.app also saves your text automatically in your browser, so you can close the tab and return later without losing your work.

## What makes freewordcounter.app useful for essay writing specifically?

freewordcounter.app provides the three most important metrics for essay writers in one view: word count, paragraph count, and sentence count. The top 10 most frequent words feature helps you identify overused terms in your writing — a common issue in essays where students unconsciously repeat the same words. Spotting and replacing repetitive words improves the quality of your prose.

The copy stats feature lets you quickly copy all your essay statistics to the clipboard, which is useful if you need to include a word count declaration at the end of your essay. The dark mode toggle is helpful for late-night writing sessions, and the font size controls let you increase the editor text size for more comfortable reading and editing. freewordcounter.app respects your privacy — your essay text stays in your browser and is never sent to any server, making it safe for academic work including exam preparation and application essays.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How do I check the word count of my essay?**
Open freewordcounter.app in any browser, paste your essay text into the editor, and your word count appears instantly in the stats panel. The count updates in real time as you edit.

**How many words should a college essay be?**
College essay word counts vary by assignment. Common lengths include 250 words (Common App short answer), 500 words (standard short essay), 650 words (Common App personal statement), 1,000-1,500 words (research essay), and 2,500-5,000 words (term paper or thesis chapter).

**Does freewordcounter.app count paragraphs in my essay?**
Yes. freewordcounter.app displays paragraph count alongside word count, character count, and sentence count. Paragraphs are detected by line breaks in your text.

**Is my essay text stored on a server?**
No. freewordcounter.app stores all text in your browser's localStorage only. Nothing is ever sent to any server. Your essay content remains private on your device.

**Can I use freewordcounter.app to check reading time for my essay?**
Yes. freewordcounter.app calculates reading time at 200 words per minute and speaking time at 130 words per minute, which is helpful for essay presentations and timed readings.

# Free Word Counter for Students

https://freewordcounter.app/word-counter-for-students.html

Students check word counts more than almost any other group of writers. Every essay, report, and assignment comes with a word limit — sometimes a minimum, sometimes a maximum, often both. freewordcounter.app is a free word counter that lets students paste their text and see an accurate word count instantly, along with character count, sentence count, paragraph count, reading time, and more. There is no login, no account creation, no ads, and no cost.

## Why do students need a dedicated word counter?

Word processors like Google Docs and Microsoft Word show word counts, but they require opening the application, creating or uploading a document, and navigating menus to find the count. freewordcounter.app is a single-purpose tool that shows your word count the instant you paste text. Students working on Chromebooks, tablets, library computers, or phones may not have access to a full word processor at all. freewordcounter.app works in any browser on any device, making it accessible regardless of the student's hardware or software situation.

freewordcounter.app also provides statistics that are specifically useful for academic writing. Paragraph count helps verify essay structure. Average sentence length reveals whether sentences are consistently too long (a common issue in academic writing) or too short. The top 10 most-used words feature exposes repetitive language, which is one of the fastest ways students can improve their writing quality.

## What word count requirements do students commonly face?

Word count requirements vary across education levels and assignment types. High school essays typically require 300 to 1,000 words. The Common Application personal statement has a 650-word maximum. College-level essays and papers range from 500 words for short responses to 5,000 words for major research papers. Graduate theses can require 10,000 to 20,000 words per chapter. freewordcounter.app handles all of these lengths without any performance issues.

Some assignments specify character counts rather than word counts. Scholarship applications and short-answer sections on standardized tests often use character limits instead. freewordcounter.app shows both character count with spaces and character count without spaces, so students always have the right number regardless of how the limit is defined.

## How does freewordcounter.app help students write better?

freewordcounter.app goes beyond simple counting to provide writing insights. The average sentence length statistic helps students aim for the 15-20 word range that most style guides recommend for clear academic prose. Sentences averaging above 25 words tend to be harder to follow, while sentences averaging below 10 words can feel disconnected.

The word frequency analysis is particularly valuable for self-editing. By showing the 10 most-used non-common words in a piece of text, freewordcounter.app helps students spot when they have overused a particular term. Replacing repetitive words with synonyms or restructuring sentences improves both readability and the impression of a broader vocabulary. The speaking time estimate, calculated at 130 words per minute, helps students who need to present their work orally, ensuring their essay or presentation fits within a time limit.

## Why is freewordcounter.app ideal for students specifically?

freewordcounter.app costs nothing, which matters for students on tight budgets. There are no premium features locked behind a paywall for core counting functionality. The tool requires no login, which means no password to remember and no account to manage. freewordcounter.app works offline after the first visit, which is essential for students working in libraries with unreliable Wi-Fi, on public transit, or in exam rooms with limited internet access.

Privacy is another important factor. freewordcounter.app stores text only in the browser's localStorage and never sends anything to a server. This means students can safely paste draft essays, personal statements, and exam preparation materials without worrying about their text being stored, indexed, or accessed by anyone else. The dark mode toggle is helpful for late-night study sessions, and the font size controls make the editor comfortable to use on screens of all sizes.

Yes. freewordcounter.app is fully responsive and works on phones, tablets, laptops, and desktops. It works in any modern browser including Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

Yes, but only in your browser's localStorage on your device. Your text is never sent to any server. You can close the tab and come back later — your text will still be there.

freewordcounter.app shows average sentence length and your top 10 most-used words, which help you identify repetitive language and sentences that are too long or too short. These metrics are useful for self-editing essays and assignments.
